source: NCERT Class X, Contemporary India II, Geography Ch. 4.

sections.heading: 1. Types of Farming
points: **Primitive subsistence farming** — 'slash and burn' on small patches using primitive tools; depends on monsoon and soil fertility; called **jhumming** (NE India), **milpa, roca** etc. elsewhere.
**Intensive subsistence farming** — labour-intensive, high doses of biochemical inputs and irrigation, on small holdings (densely populated areas).
**Commercial farming** — high use of modern inputs (HYV seeds, fertilisers) for market; includes **plantation** farming (single crop like tea, coffee, rubber on large estates).

sections.heading: 2. Cropping Seasons
points: **Rabi** — sown in winter (Oct–Dec), harvested in summer (Apr–Jun): **wheat, barley, peas, gram, mustard**.
**Kharif** — sown with the monsoon (Jun–Jul), harvested Sep–Oct: **rice, maize, jowar, bajra, tur, cotton, jute, groundnut**.
**Zaid** — short summer season (between rabi and kharif): **watermelon, muskmelon, cucumber, vegetables, fodder**.

sections.heading: 3. Major Crops
points: **Rice** — staple food; needs high temperature, high humidity, rainfall >100 cm (or irrigation); grown in plains, NE, coasts, deltas.
**Wheat** — main rabi crop; needs cool growing season, bright sunshine at ripening; grown in Ganga-Satluj plains and Deccan black soil.
**Millets** — jowar, bajra, ragi (coarse grains, high nutrition).
**Pulses** — major source of protein; India is the largest producer and consumer; **leguminous** crops fix nitrogen.
**Sugarcane, oilseeds (groundnut, mustard), tea, coffee, horticulture (India = 2nd largest producer of fruits/vegetables)**.
**Non-food crops**: rubber, cotton (kharif, black soil), jute ('golden fibre', Bengal/Assam).

sections.heading: 4. Reforms and Institutional Support
points: **Green Revolution** and **White Revolution (Operation Flood)** modernised agriculture.
**Land reforms** (1960s–70s): 'land to the tiller', consolidation of holdings, abolition of zamindari.
Government support: **minimum support price (MSP)**, subsidies on inputs, Kisan Credit Card (KCC), crop insurance, Grameen banks.
Institutions like **ICAR**, agricultural universities, weather bulletins and **'Operation Flood'** aid farmers.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Jhumming = slash-and-burn (NE India); milpa (Mexico), roca (Brazil).
Rabi = winter-sown (wheat); Kharif = monsoon-sown (rice); Zaid = summer.
Rice needs >100 cm rain; wheat = rabi, Ganga-Satluj plains.
Jute = 'golden fibre'; India = largest producer/consumer of pulses.
White Revolution = Operation Flood (milk).

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Rabi** crops are **sown in winter, harvested in summer** (wheat); **Kharif** with the monsoon (rice).
**Jhumming** = **slash-and-burn** (primitive subsistence, NE India).
**Jute** is the **'golden fibre'**; **millets** are coarse grains (jowar/bajra/ragi).
India is the **largest producer and consumer of pulses**.
